{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "observations": [
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_def_1",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "Depth-first search is a search algorithm that considers outgoing edges (children) of a vertex before any of the vertex's siblings (outgoing edges of the vertex's predecessor in the search).",
      "start_line": 5,
      "end_line": 13
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_extremes",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "In depth-first search, extremes are searched first.",
      "start_line": 13,
      "end_line": 13
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_recursion",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "Depth-first search is easily implemented with recursion.",
      "start_line": 13,
      "end_line": 14
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_def_2",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "Depth-first search is an algorithm that marks all vertices in a directed graph in the order they are discovered and finished, partitioning the graph into a forest.",
      "start_line": 15,
      "end_line": 19
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_alias",
      "facet": "term",
      "statement": "Depth-first search is also known as DFS.",
      "start_line": 20,
      "end_line": 21
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_specializations",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Preorder traversal, in-order traversal, and postorder traversal are specializations of depth-first search.",
      "start_line": 22,
      "end_line": 29
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_timing_ambiguity",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "Depth-first search does not specify if a vertex is considered before, during, or after its outgoing edges or children.",
      "start_line": 40,
      "end_line": 40
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_dfs_traversal_types",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Because of the timing ambiguity, depth-first search can be preorder, in-order, or postorder traversal.",
      "start_line": 40,
      "end_line": 46
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_ref_clr",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "CLR90, pages 477-485 is a reference for depth-first search.",
      "start_line": 47,
      "end_line": 47
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_impl_java_cpp",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "Algorithms and Data Structures provides explanation and implementation (Java and C++) for undirected graphs.",
      "start_line": 50,
      "end_line": 54
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_impl_sedgewick",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "Sedgewick and Wayne 'Algorithms' 4th edition provides many algorithms using depth-first search (Java).",
      "start_line": 54,
      "end_line": 55
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_ref_green_raphael",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "C. Cordell Green and Bertram Raphael, 'The use of theorem-proving techniques in question-answering systems', Proc. 1968 23rd ACM national conference, pages 169-181, 1968, is an early mention of depth-first search.",
      "start_line": 65,
      "end_line": 72
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_ref_golomb_baumert",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "Solomon W. Golomb and Leonard D. Baumert, 'Backtrack Programming', Journal of ACM, 12(4):516-524, Oct 1965, is an earlier description of what would be called depth-first search with pruning of infeasible solutions.",
      "start_line": 73,
      "end_line": 79
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_related_bfs",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Breadth-first search is related to depth-first search.",
      "start_line": 31,
      "end_line": 31
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_related_best_first",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Best-first search is related to depth-first search.",
      "start_line": 33,
      "end_line": 33
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_related_schorr_waite",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Schorr-Waite graph marking algorithm is related to depth-first search.",
      "start_line": 35,
      "end_line": 35
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_related_cupif_giannini",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Cupif-Giannini tree traversal is related to depth-first search.",
      "start_line": 37,
      "end_line": 37
    }
  ],
  "claims": [],
  "questions": []
}
